# Delivery Gates Checklist: Restore Main CI

**Purpose**: Validate that the requirements for the CI repair are complete, clear, consistent, and measurable before delivery.
**Created**: 2026-10-16
**Feature**: [spec.md](spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Is a requirement stated for each of the five causes found, so that none of them depends on an unstated fix? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001, §FR-006, §FR-007, §FR-009, §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK002 Are the Pi releases the typecheck must pass against named explicitly rather than as "current"? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK003 Is the expected behavior of a user-prompt run stated alongside the custom-run behavior, so that the narrowing cannot silently change it? [Coverage, Spec §US1 scenario 3]
- [ ] CHK004 Are requirements defined for a custom run that is not the queued processing request? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK005 Is the handling of a Pi release newer than the one tested stated, including that CI keeps installing it unpinned? [Dependency, Spec §Edge Cases, §Assumptions]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK006 Is "interrupt the drain only while it is parked at its delay" defined by an observable condition rather than by timing? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK007 Is the bound on the wait for the parked drain stated, together with what the failure must name? [Measurability, Spec §US4 scenario 2]
- [ ] CHK008 Is "stalls the host" in the OpenCode requirement tied to a purpose and not only to a duration? [Clarity, Spec §US5]
- [ ] CHK009 Is it clear that the contributions fixture is restored to the upstream version and not merged with the older lock-based helper? [Clarity, Spec §Assumptions]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK010 Do FR-010 (no weakened tests) and the stimulus change of the processing-request case agree, with the change justified in the artifacts? [Consistency, Spec §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK011 Does the statement that no supervision behavior changes beyond the named requirements agree with the OpenCode requirement added later? [Conflict, Spec §FR-011, §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK012 Do the success criteria for the drain (1500 runs) and the plan's verification (1727 runs) use the same definition of an unexpected success? [Consistency, Spec §SC-004]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK013 Can SC-001 (all eighteen jobs pass) be judged from one CI run, and is the run it applies to identified? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK014 Is the baseline for each repeat-count criterion recorded so the improvement is measurable? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004, §SC-006]
- [ ] CHK015 Is each acceptance scenario traceable to a behavior and a test through the test list? [Traceability, Spec §User Scenarios]

## Scope and Boundaries

- [ ] CHK016 Are the sibling stdin writes and the locale-dependent coverage guard recorded as out of scope with a reason instead of left unmentioned? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK017 Is the exclusion of version pinning stated with the reason, so a reviewer can challenge it? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]

## Dependencies and Assumptions

- [ ] CHK018 Is the assumption that bash 5.2 loses the trap marked as inferred from the error text and not proven? [Assumption, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK019 Are the tools the verification depends on (scratch Pi installs, bash 5.2 container) listed so that the evidence can be repeated? [Dependency, Gap]

## Notes

Reviewers own checklist markers; `/speckit-implement` reads checklist state and does not modify markers.
Items CHK001 to CHK019 are open for the reviewer; the delivery pipeline's review and the operator are the intended reviewers.
